answer.evidence: radon/metrics.py:150-157 defines mi_rank(score) as chr(65 + (9 - score >= 0) + (19 - score >= 0)). At score 9 both comparisons are true, giving 'C'. At 19 only the second is true, giving 'B'. Above 19 it gives 'A'. This matches the docstring (A if >19, B if 9<score<=19, C if <=9), so the boundaries are inclusive on the lower grade. The review should check that boolean arithmetic on chr() is readable and handles float scores at the edges. It should also check that callers pass the raw MI value, not a clamped or rounded one. radon/raw.py and radon/visitors.py feed the inputs to the MI calculation (LOC counts and complexity or Halstead data), so I would review how those values are produced and whether they could shift a score across a threshold. radon/complexity.py has its own rank logic for cyclomatic complexity, which is unrelated to the MI thresholds, so it only needs a quick look.
